questions.prompt: Every express delivery pays a fee. Every large parcel requires a van. Vans cannot operate on weekends. Which weekend delivery could obey all three rules?

options.text: A large express parcel, fee paid, carried by van.
A small express parcel, no fee, carried by bicycle.
A small express parcel, fee paid, carried by bicycle.
A large regular parcel carried by bicycle.

questions.explanation: The small express bicycle delivery pays its required fee and needs no van. The alternatives violate the weekend van restriction, express fee rule, or large-parcel van requirement.

questions.prompt: Four jobs A, B, C and D fill four slots. B is immediately before D, and A is before B. If D is first, C is last; otherwise C is first. Which order satisfies every rule?
questions.explanation: D cannot be first because B must precede it. Therefore C is first, leaving A before the consecutive pair B, D.

questions.prompt: A workshop uses either an electric press or a hand press. Electric use requires both a charged battery and a safety screen. Hand use requires a clamp. The battery is empty, while the screen and clamp are available. Which conclusion follows?

options.text: Only the electric press meets its requirements
Only the hand press meets its requirements

questions.explanation: The empty battery rules out the electric press even though its screen is available. The hand press’s stated clamp requirement is met.

questions.prompt: A machine begins with either 4 or 7 tokens. An even starting number is doubled; an odd starting number gains 3. The machine then removes 2 tokens. Its final count is even and greater than 7. What was its starting count?
questions.explanation: Starting with 4 gives 8, then 6, which is too small. Starting with 7 gives 10, then 8, satisfying both final conditions.

questions.prompt: A parcel travels by rail or road. Every rail parcel is sealed. No sealed parcel contains loose sand. Every road parcel has a red label. This parcel contains loose sand. Which feature must it have?
questions.explanation: Loose sand excludes a seal, and therefore excludes rail. The parcel must travel by road, whose parcels all have red labels.

questions.prompt: Only Mina, Omar and Pia race, without ties. Either Mina or Omar finishes first. If Mina is first, Pia beats Omar. If Omar finishes first, Mina finishes immediately after him. Pia is not last. What is the finishing order?
questions.explanation: Omar first would put Mina second and Pia last, contradicting the clue. Mina must be first, and Pia must precede Omar.

questions.prompt: Boxes X and Y contain one blue token and one red token, one per box. A tester starts X’s reading at 2 and Y’s at 5. It adds 2 for blue and subtracts 1 for red. The final readings match. Which arrangement fits?
questions.explanation: X blue and Y red produce readings 4 and 4. Reversing the colours produces 1 and 7, so the matching readings identify the first arrangement.

questions.prompt: A badge is either silver or gold. A silver badge qualifies only when it has exactly two stripes; a gold badge qualifies only when it has a star. This qualifying badge has three stripes and no star is visible because that area is covered. What must be covered?
questions.explanation: Three stripes prevent a silver badge from qualifying. The qualifying badge must be gold, and gold qualification requires a star in the covered area.

questions.prompt: A delivery uses the tunnel or bridge, with only these restrictions: the tunnel allows at most 6 crates and requires a small van; the bridge requires a permit. You have 7 crates, a small van and no permit. Which single change makes a route possible?

options.text: Replace the small van with a bicycle

questions.explanation: Seven crates rule out the tunnel despite the small van. A permit alone makes the bridge available without changing the load.

questions.prompt: A lock opens with either a blue key plus code 8, or a green key plus code 3. Exactly one opening combination is available. You have both keys, but code 8 is unavailable. What must also be available?
questions.explanation: The blue-key combination fails without code 8. Since one complete opening combination is available, the green key must be paired with code 3.

questions.prompt: A ticket is valid exactly when it has either stamp+date or barcode+signature. Every dated ticket has a batch number. This ticket has a stamp and barcode but no batch number; its signature area is covered. Which check decides whether it is valid?

options.text: Recheck whether it has a stamp
Check whether its paper is blue
Check whether it has a signature

questions.explanation: No batch number rules out a date, so stamp+date cannot apply. The barcode is present, leaving the signature as the deciding requirement for the remaining route.

questions.prompt: Four runners finish without ties. If Sol beats Tai, Uma is first; otherwise Vic is first. Sol finishes third, and Uma finishes second. Who must finish first?
questions.explanation: Uma is not first, so the Sol-beats-Tai case is impossible. Tai must beat Sol, and the other case requires Vic first.

questions.prompt: A display contains exactly two of A, B and C. If A is included, B must be excluded. If A is excluded, C must be excluded. Which display is possible?
questions.explanation: Excluding A also excludes C, leaving too few objects. Including A excludes B, so the required second object is C.

questions.prompt: A counter starts at either 2 or 5. Pressing P adds 4 if the starting value is below 4; otherwise it subtracts 1. Pressing Q then triples the result. The final value is below 15. Which starting value fits?
questions.explanation: Starting at 2 leads to 6 and then 18. Starting at 5 leads to 4 and then 12, the only result below 15.

questions.prompt: Every member of a club belongs to exactly one team: North or South. All North members train on Tuesday. No Tuesday trainee has a weekend shift. Leena has a weekend shift and belongs to the club. Which team is hers?
questions.explanation: A weekend shift excludes Tuesday training, which all North members have. Because Leena belongs to exactly one of the two teams, she is South.

questions.prompt: A file is accepted through either rule X or rule Y. X requires a short name and a checksum. Y requires a long name and a signature. The file is accepted, its name is long, and names cannot be both lengths. What is required?
questions.explanation: The long name prevents acceptance through X. Acceptance must therefore use Y, which requires both the long name and a signature.

questions.prompt: Exactly one of two lamps, A or B, is on. If A is on, the fan runs and the door is shut. If B is on, the fan stops. The door is open. What must be true?

options.text: A is on and the fan runs
B is on and the fan stops
B is on and the fan runs

questions.explanation: An open door contradicts the consequence of A being on. Therefore B is the one illuminated lamp, and its rule stops the fan.

questions.prompt: A team can use plan Red or Blue. Red needs two editors and no translator. Blue needs one editor and one translator. Only one editor is available, and exactly one plan can be staffed. What else must be available?
questions.explanation: One editor cannot staff Red. Since a plan can be staffed, it must be Blue, requiring a translator alongside that editor.

questions.prompt: A device is in mode A or B. In A, its badge is triangular and its gate opens. In B, its badge is circular and its gate closes. Every circular badge has etching. The device’s badge is unetched. Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: The unetched badge cannot be circular, eliminating mode B. Since exactly one of the two modes applies, the device is in A and its gate opens.

questions.prompt: An exhibit uses either order A–B–C–D or D–C–B–A before removing one item. The remaining items keep their relative order. A is removed, and B is observed before C. Which item is now last?
questions.explanation: Only the forward order places B before C. Removing A from that order leaves B, C, D, making D last.

questions.prompt: Two routes have only these requirements: fast needs working cooling; slow needs insulation and a journey of at most four hours. Cooling works only with power, which is off. The slow journey has two 90-minute legs. Which remaining check decides whether delivery is possible?

options.text: Whether the fast route is shorter
Whether the slow route has two legs
Whether the cooling unit has a label

questions.explanation: No power rules out working cooling and thus the fast route. The slow trip totals three hours, meeting its time limit; insulation is its only unresolved requirement.

questions.prompt: A positive whole number gains 3. If the result is even, it is halved; otherwise it gains 5. Finally, 2 is subtracted. The final result is 6. What was the starting number?
questions.explanation: Before subtraction the value was 8. The even branch therefore began at 16, giving start 13. The odd branch would require start 0, which is excluded.

questions.prompt: Five tasks D, E, F, G and H occupy five slots. H must finish last, F immediately precedes H, G precedes F, and E is between D and G. Which task must occupy slot 2?
questions.explanation: H and F fill slots 5 and 4. D, E and G occupy the first three slots. E must be between the other two, placing it second.

questions.prompt: Every finalist passed screening. Everyone who passed screening submitted a sample. No anonymous submission included a sample. Some finalists received prizes. What must be true of every prize-winning finalist?

options.text: Their sample received the highest score

questions.explanation: Finalist status implies passing screening and submitting a sample. Because anonymous submissions never include samples, a prize-winning finalist cannot have submitted anonymously.

questions.prompt: A green status appears only when both review and upload are complete. Upload can finish only after compression, and compression requires the source file. Green status is now visible. What must already have been available?
questions.explanation: Work backward from green status to completed upload, then compression. Compression requires the source file, so that file must have been available.

questions.prompt: A parcel must arrive by 18:00. Travel takes 2 hours, packing takes 30 minutes and inspection takes 45 minutes. Inspection must finish before packing starts; packing must finish before travel. With no waiting, what is the latest inspection start?
questions.explanation: Travel must start by 16:00, so packing starts by 15:30. Subtracting the 45-minute inspection gives a latest start of 14:45.

questions.prompt: A borrowing analysis must use consistent loan categories, unchanged stock, and before-and-after comparison with a control branch. Stock was unchanged, but digital loans were newly included in reported totals. Both branches have physical-loan records for both periods. Which analysis meets all three checks?

options.text: Compare total-loan changes between the two branches
Compare physical-loan changes between the two branches
Compare only the main branch’s physical-loan change
Compare only the branches’ later physical-loan counts

questions.explanation: Physical-only records restore consistent categories. Comparing each branch’s before-and-after change supplies the control comparison, while unchanged stock already satisfies the remaining requirement.

questions.prompt: A code qualifies only if it has three different digits, its last digit is twice its first, and its digit sum is 10. The middle digit is 4. Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: The first and last digits must sum to 6 and have a two-to-one relationship, forcing 2 and 4. That repeats the middle digit, violating distinctness.

questions.prompt: A team needs a writer, editor and designer, with different people in each role. Jo can write or edit; Kai can edit or design; Luz can only write. To staff all three roles, which role must Kai take?
questions.explanation: Luz must be the writer. That leaves Jo to edit, since Jo cannot design, so Kai must be the designer.

questions.prompt: You need 12 finished panels. Cutting produces two blanks per sheet. Each finished panel uses one blank, and four blanks are reserved for testing. Sheets are sold in packs of three. What is the smallest number of packs needed?
questions.explanation: Twelve panels plus four test blanks require 16 blanks, or eight sheets. Two packs contain only six sheets; three packs provide nine.

questions.prompt: A school reported 30 late arrivals before and 20 afterward. The earlier cutoff was 09:05; 12 of those 30 arrived by 09:10, the later cutoff. A control school using 09:10 throughout rose from 10 to 12. What does a common-cutoff comparison show?

options.text: The first school improved by ten arrivals
Both schools’ late-arrival counts increased by two
The first school improved by twelve arrivals
The control school’s late-arrival count stayed unchanged

questions.explanation: At 09:10, the first school’s earlier late count is 30−12=18, rising to 20. The control rises from 10 to 12, the same increase of two.

questions.prompt: A three-letter code is reversed, its first letter moves one place forward alphabetically, and its last letter moves one place backward. No wraparound occurs. The result is DBC. What was the original code?
questions.explanation: Undo the last-letter change to get DBD, then undo the first-letter change to get CBD. Reversing CBD recovers DBC.

questions.prompt: All premium records are verified. Every verified record has an owner. No ownerless record is searchable. A premium record is missing from search results. Which conclusion is still guaranteed?
questions.explanation: Premium status guarantees verification and therefore an owner. The search rule excludes ownerless records but does not promise that every owned record is searchable.

questions.prompt: A rover must finish with at least 3 energy units. The final drive costs 5, the preceding scan costs 4, and a charging stop before both adds exactly 6. What minimum energy must it have just before charging?
questions.explanation: The rover needs 12 units after charging to spend 9 and retain 3. Since charging adds 6, it must arrive with at least 6.

questions.prompt: Five books A–E stand in a row. C is third, B immediately precedes C, E is after C, and D is immediately after E. Which book must stand first?
questions.explanation: C fixes B in position 2. E and D must fill positions 4 and 5 in that order, leaving A in position 1.

questions.prompt: An accepted design must be symmetric, use at most three colours, and have a border if it contains a circle. A symmetric circular design already uses three colours but has no border. Which single revision can make it meet all requirements?

options.text: Add a symmetric border using an existing colour
Add a border in a fourth colour
Add a fourth colour without a border

questions.explanation: The missing border is the unsatisfied requirement. Reusing an existing colour adds the border while preserving symmetry and the three-colour limit.

questions.prompt: Publication is allowed exactly when approval is granted and upload is complete. Approval occurs exactly when review and disclosure are complete. Upload completes exactly when compression is done and the checksum passes. Review and compression are done; disclosure is missing and the checksum fails. Which pair of repairs permits publication?

options.text: Repeat review and pass the checksum
Complete disclosure and pass the checksum

questions.explanation: Trace both publication requirements backward. Approval still lacks disclosure, while upload still lacks a passing checksum. Repairing those two gaps completes both prerequisite branches.

questions.prompt: Release is allowed exactly when encryption and verification are complete. Verification succeeds through either checksum+audit or matching mirror+signature. A signature is added exactly when reviewers R and S agree. Encryption, audit and mirror matching are complete; checksum failed. R agrees. What remaining event permits release?

options.text: The failed checksum is ignored without a signature

questions.explanation: The failed checksum blocks one verification route. The matching mirror leaves a signature necessary, and the signature rule now lacks only S’s agreement because R already agrees.

questions.prompt: Equal-arm scales balance three identical blocks plus 2 weight units against one identical block plus 10 weight units. How many of these blocks have a total weight of 16 units?
questions.explanation: Removing one block from each side leaves two blocks balancing 8 units. Each block weighs 4 units, so four blocks weigh 16 units.

questions.prompt: Only registered entries can reach the final round. Registration requires both a name and a contact address. An entry reached the final round without a phone number. Which information must it nevertheless have supplied?

options.text: A phone number and a name
A name and a contact address

questions.explanation: Reaching the final implies registration. Registration in turn requires both a name and a contact address; no rule requires a phone number.

questions.prompt: To isolate quiet rooms’ effect on puzzle accuracy, a study must avoid group selection, puzzle-difficulty differences and unequal practice. Current volunteers choose their room; quiet-room users get easier puzzles and more practice. Which redesign addresses all three obstacles?

options.text: Let volunteers choose rooms; use identical puzzles and equal practice
Randomize rooms; keep different puzzles and equal practice
Randomize rooms; use identical puzzles and equal practice
Randomize rooms; use identical puzzles but extra quiet-room practice

questions.explanation: Random assignment addresses selection, identical puzzles control difficulty, and equal practice controls preparation. Each other proposal leaves one of those stated obstacles in place.

questions.prompt: Choose exactly two projects within a 7-credit budget. A costs 4 and earns 9 points but requires B. B costs 3 and earns 5; C costs 5 and earns 8; D costs 2 and earns 4. Which pair earns most?
questions.explanation: A and D violate A’s dependency. B and D earn 9, and C and D earn 12. A and B fit the budget and earn 14.

questions.prompt: Three jobs run consecutively without overlap or idle time. A takes 3 minutes, B takes 1 and C takes 2. B must precede C. Starting at minute 0, which order minimizes the sum of the three completion times?
questions.explanation: B, C, A finishes jobs at minutes 1, 3 and 6, totaling 10. The other valid orders total 13 and 11; C first violates the precedence rule.

questions.prompt: Four tests detect these fault types: A detects 1, 2, 3; B detects 3, 4; C detects 1, 4, 5; D detects 2, 5. You can run two tests. Which pair covers the greatest number of distinct types?
questions.explanation: A and C together cover all five types. Each other listed pair misses at least one type, so none matches that coverage.

questions.prompt: You must carry 10 identical items. Large boxes hold 6 and cost 7 credits; medium boxes hold 4 and cost 4; small boxes hold 3 and cost 4. Any number is available, and unused capacity is allowed. What is the cheapest purchase?

options.text: One large and one medium box
Two medium and one small box

questions.explanation: One large plus one medium provides exactly 10 spaces for 11 credits. Two medium boxes are insufficient; every sufficient all-medium or small-box alternative costs at least 12.

questions.prompt: Choose an entry scoring at least 8 with no more than two errors. Prefer fewer errors, then lower cost. A: score 9, errors 2, cost 3. B: 8, 1, 5. C: 7, 0, 1. D: 8, 1, 4. Which wins?
questions.explanation: C fails the score threshold. B and D beat A on errors; their error counts tie, so D wins on its lower cost.

questions.prompt: One of four models A–D is correct. Test X distinguishes AB from CD and costs 2. Y distinguishes AC from BD and costs 3. Z distinguishes A from BCD and costs 1. Results are exact. Which bundle identifies the model at lowest total cost?
questions.explanation: X and Y give each model a unique pair of results for cost 5. X with Z leaves C/D unresolved; Y with Z leaves B/D unresolved.

questions.prompt: Rank programs by score increase minus the control group’s 5-point increase; break ties by lower cost. A rises 40→60 and costs 5. B rises 55→70 and costs 2. C rises 30→50 and costs 3. Which program ranks first?
questions.explanation: A and C each gain 20, or 15 beyond the control increase. B gains only 10 beyond control. C wins the A/C tie because it costs less.

questions.prompt: One room hosts non-overlapping sessions. P runs 09:00–10:00 for 4 points; Q runs 09:30–11:00 for 7; R runs 10:00–11:00 for 4; S runs 11:00–12:00 for 2. Back-to-back sessions are allowed. Which selection maximizes points?
questions.explanation: P and R fit consecutively and earn 8, beating Q’s 7 over that period. S fits afterward, bringing the maximum total to 10.

questions.prompt: A counter starts at 2. You must use +3, ×2 and −1 exactly once each. Multiplication cannot be last. Which operation order produces the largest final number?
questions.explanation: Adding before multiplication doubles the added 3, while subtracting afterward loses only 1. This gives 9; the other listed valid orders give 6, 6 and 5.

questions.prompt: Allocate nine identical tokens among three teams. Each needs at least two. First maximize the smallest allocation; if several allocations tie, maximize Team A’s allocation. Which allocation to A, B and C wins?
questions.explanation: A minimum above 3 would require at least 12 tokens. Achieving minimum 3 uses all nine as 3, 3, 3, so no tie-break is needed.

questions.prompt: Choose the smallest four-digit code with different digits, no zero, an even final digit, and a digit sum of 12. Which code meets the objective?
questions.explanation: Start with the smallest possible digits, 1 then 2. Choosing 3 next forces the final digit to be 6, which is distinct and even. Thus 1236 is minimal.

questions.prompt: A kit needs at least one writing tool and one measuring tool. Pencil P costs 2 and writes; ruler R costs 3 and measures; multi-tool M costs 6 and does both; pen N costs 4 and writes. No other tools exist. What is the cheapest complete kit?
questions.explanation: P and R cover both required functions for 5 credits. M alone costs 6, while substituting N or adding M costs more.

questions.prompt: A four-cell row must contain one red cell and three blue cells. You may inspect individual cells. You must guarantee detecting any violation, including an extra red cell. What is the smallest worst-case number of inspections?
questions.explanation: After three inspections, an unchecked cell can still change a valid row into an invalid one. Inspecting all four guarantees detection and is necessary in the worst case.

questions.prompt: A study must randomize groups, equalize practice and measure before and after. Design A does all three for 8 credits. B randomizes and equalizes but measures only afterward, costing 4. C measures both times with equal practice but self-selected groups, costing 3. D does all three for 6. Which qualifying design is cheapest?
questions.explanation: B lacks baseline measurement and C lacks random assignment. A and D meet every design requirement, but D costs 6 rather than 8 credits.

questions.prompt: Each red model uses 2 wood units and earns 5 points. Each blue model uses 3 wood units and earns 8 points. You have 8 wood units and must make at least one of each. Which production plan earns most?
questions.explanation: One red and two blue use all 8 units and earn 21. Two red and one blue earn 18; three red and one blue exceed the supply.

questions.prompt: A route starts at S, visits K before L, and ends at T. Directed road times are S→K:4, S→M:1, M→K:1, K→L:2, L→T:2, K→N:1, N→L:2, M→L:1. No other roads exist. Which route is shortest while meeting the checkpoint rule?
questions.explanation: S→M→K→L→T takes 1+1+2+2=6 minutes. The other valid choices take 8 and 9; the tempting 4-minute route through M skips K.

questions.prompt: Cards read D, B, A, C, E. One move swaps adjacent cards. A must precede B, B must precede D, C must precede D, and E must stay last. Which valid final order requires the fewest moves?
questions.explanation: A,B,C,D,E needs four swaps; the other valid listed orders need five and six. A,C,D,B,E puts D before B, violating an unchanged ordering requirement.

questions.prompt: Choosing A guarantees B; B guarantees C. Choosing D guarantees C and E. Nothing else follows. You may choose one starting letter. Which choice guarantees the most distinct letters, counting the starting letter, with ties favouring the alphabetically earlier choice?
questions.explanation: A guarantees A, B and C; D guarantees D, C and E. Both reach three letters, so the stated alphabetical tie-break selects A.

questions.prompt: Choose a plan by maximizing its lowest payoff across rain and sun; break ties using the higher sunny payoff. Plan A pays 6/6, B pays 4/10, C pays 6/8, and D pays 5/9, listed as rain/sun. Which plan wins?
questions.explanation: The minimum payoffs are 6, 4, 6 and 5. A and C tie for the best minimum, and C wins because its sunny payoff is 8 rather than 6.

questions.prompt: Exactly one of eight numbered boxes contains a token. A check tells you whether the token is in any chosen group of boxes. Every check is reliable. What is the fewest checks that guarantees locating the token?
questions.explanation: Each yes/no check can at most double distinguishable outcomes. Two checks cover only four boxes; three balanced splits can distinguish all eight.

questions.prompt: A code is 124, 142, 214, 241 or 412. Its first digit is not 4. You may request one pair of observations. Which pair always identifies the surviving code?

options.text: First digit and whether the middle digit is even

questions.explanation: The clue leaves four codes. Their first/last pairs are 1/4, 1/2, 2/4 and 2/1, all distinct. Each other observation pair leaves at least two codes indistinguishable.

questions.prompt: Exactly two of A, B, C and D are selected. A is selected if and only if B is. If A is absent, C is present. Which question distinguishes all remaining possibilities?

options.text: Is at least one of A or C selected?
Is at least one of B or D selected?

questions.explanation: The only possibilities are A/B together or C/D together. A’s presence distinguishes them, while each other question has the same answer for both.

questions.prompt: A toy alarm sounds with both a dim battery and a blocked sensor. One proposed model says only battery state matters; another says only blockage matters. Each model predicts silence when its cause is removed. Which test separates the models?

options.text: Replace the battery and clear the sensor together
Fit a charged battery while keeping the sensor blocked
Measure the alarm’s current volume again

questions.explanation: Battery replacement alone predicts silence under the battery model and continued sound under the blockage model. Changing both conditions would make both models predict silence.

questions.prompt: A, B, C and D occupy four slots. A immediately precedes B, C immediately precedes D, and the two pairs do not overlap. Which single check distinguishes the two possible orders?
questions.explanation: The two intact pairs can appear as A, B, C, D or C, D, A, B. Only the position of A differs among the offered checks.

questions.prompt: A kit contains blocks weighing either 3+3, 2+2+2, 1+1+4 or 4+4 units. Its measured weight is 6. Which pair of exact observations always identifies its contents?

options.text: Block count and whether all blocks have equal weight
Block count and whether any blocks are present

questions.explanation: The weight excludes 4+4. Of the survivors, 3+3 has two blocks; the others have three. Equal-weight status then separates 2+2+2 from 1+1+4.

questions.prompt: Participants using a study app score higher, but they also study longer. Two explanations remain: the app helps, or extra study time explains the difference. Which result would most strengthen an independent app effect?

options.text: Randomized app users improve more than controls given equal study time
App users report liking the app
High scorers are more likely to download the app

questions.explanation: Random assignment reduces selection bias, and equal study time controls extra practice. Greater improvement in app users therefore supports an app-specific effect.

questions.prompt: A processor applies either “add 2, then double” or “double, then add 4.” Both give 10 from input 3. You may test any whole-number input and see only the final output. Which strategy distinguishes the processors?

options.text: No input can distinguish them using final output alone

questions.explanation: The first processor returns 2(x + 2), which equals 2x + 4, exactly the second processor’s output. They agree for every permitted input.

questions.prompt: A finite collection has 100 cards. Either all red cards are round, or at least one red card is square. Each card has exactly one shape: round or square. Which inspection guarantees deciding between these claims?

options.text: Check the shape of every red card
Check whether any round card exists

questions.explanation: One square red card establishes the second claim. If every red card is checked and none is square, the first claim holds, including when no red cards exist.

questions.prompt: An initial queue is ACBD, BCAD, CABD or DCBA. A is before D. The first and third people swap. Which pair of observed positions in the new queue always identifies the initial queue?

options.text: First and whether D is last

questions.explanation: The clue excludes DCBA. The remaining queues become BCAD, ACBD and BACD. Their first two people differ as pairs; each other offered check leaves a shared result.

questions.prompt: A machine follows either y = 2x + 3 or y = 3x + 1. Both give 7 for input 2. You may choose one input from 0, 2, or “repeat 2 twice.” Which test provides different predictions?

options.text: All listed tests give different predictions

questions.explanation: Input 0 gives 3 under the first rule and 1 under the second. Repeating input 2 only repeats the shared prediction of 7.

questions.prompt: A plan lists crossings for clear/rainy/windy days. A:bridge/tunnel/ferry; B:bridge/ferry/tunnel; C:bridge/tunnel/tunnel; D:ferry/bridge/tunnel. A clear-day delivery used the bridge. Which pair of further observed crossings always identifies the plan?
questions.explanation: The clear-day result excludes D. A, B and C predict distinct rainy/windy pairs, while either weather result alone leaves two plans sharing the same prediction.

questions.prompt: A town’s recycling rises after new bins arrive and collection becomes weekly. The council wants to separate the bin effect from the collection-frequency effect. Which additional comparison most directly does that?

options.text: The town’s recycling before both changes
Similar areas with equal collection frequency but different bins
Areas with different bins and different collection frequencies

questions.explanation: Keeping collection frequency equal removes the stated competing explanation. Comparing areas that differ in bins then provides more informative evidence about the bins themselves.

questions.prompt: Four boxes contain exactly two red and two blue tokens, one per box. A sensor reports boxes 1 and 2 red; exactly one of those reports is wrong. Direct inspection is reliable. Which two-box inspection always determines all four colours?

options.text: No two-box inspection can guarantee it

questions.explanation: Exactly one red token is in boxes 1/2, leaving one red in boxes 3/4. Inspecting one box from each pair determines its partner as the opposite colour.

questions.prompt: A 24-credit bill contains at most two items. Possible explanations are A:one 20-credit item plus 20%; B:two 12-credit items, no surcharge; C:two 10-credit items plus 20%; D:three 8-credit items, no surcharge. Which pair of fields always identifies the valid explanation?
questions.explanation: The item limit excludes D. A, B and C have count/rate pairs 1/20%, 2/0% and 2/20%, so both fields distinguish them. All share the same total.

questions.prompt: A permit is valid exactly when signed and either stamped or verified. Possible signed/stamped/verified records are A:yes/yes/no, B:yes/no/yes, C:yes/yes/yes, D:no/yes/yes. The permit is valid. Which pair of checks always identifies its record?
questions.explanation: Validity eliminates D. A, B and C all share signing and validity, but their stamping/verification pairs are yes/no, no/yes and yes/yes, uniquely distinguishing them.

questions.prompt: A map has roads S→A and B→T. Its only other road is either A→B or B→A. There are no alternative connections. Which route test distinguishes the maps?
questions.explanation: A→B creates S→A→B→T. B→A does not let S continue to T. The other reachability answers are identical under both maps.

questions.prompt: A marker starts at 1, 2, 4 or 5 on a six-position clockwise circle. Its start is below 5. It moves two steps clockwise, then one counterclockwise. Which pair of observations always identifies the start?

options.text: Final parity and whether the final position is below 6
Whether the final position exceeds 3 and exceeds 1
Whether the final position exceeds 1 and is below 6
Final parity and whether the final position exceeds 3

questions.explanation: The start is 1, 2 or 4, producing final positions 2, 3 or 5. Their parity/above-3 pairs are even/no, odd/no and odd/yes; the other pairs fail to separate them.

questions.prompt: A club gained exactly 30 members. Four accounts give invitations/acceptance rate: A:150/20%; B:100/30%; C:120/25%; D:100/20%. Each acceptance produces one new member. Exactly one account is correct. Which pair of yes/no checks distinguishes every account still possible?
questions.explanation: D predicts only 20 members and is excluded. A, B and C give above-100/above-130 pairs yes/yes, no/no and yes/no; each other pair leaves an ambiguity.

questions.prompt: A hidden rule either doubles even inputs and adds 2 to odd inputs, or adds 2 to every input. Input 2 gives 4 under both. Which next input distinguishes the rules?
questions.explanation: Odd inputs receive the same addition under both rules, and input 2 also agrees. Input 4 gives 8 under the parity rule but 6 under add-2.

questions.prompt: A display’s low attendance may reflect low interest or poor visibility. A survey finds high interest among people who noticed it, but says nothing about those who did not. Which additional evidence best tests the poor-visibility explanation?

options.text: More opinions from people already attending
Attendance after random assignment to clearer versus unchanged signs

questions.explanation: Randomly comparing clearer signs with unchanged signs directly varies visibility. An attendance difference would be informative about visibility’s role; surveying existing attendees alone misses unseen visitors.

questions.prompt: Jobs read A, B, C, D, E, F. A must precede D, B precede E, and C precede F; F stays last. New rules require C before A and E before D. Using adjacent swaps, which listed valid revision needs the fewest moves?

options.text: C, B, A, E, D, F
C, A, B, E, D, F
C, B, E, A, D, F
C, A, B, D, E, F

questions.explanation: C,A,B,E,D,F takes three swaps; the other valid listed orders take four and five. C,A,B,D,E,F violates the new E-before-D requirement.

questions.prompt: A plan must buy A, one structural check (B or C), and one electrical check (D or E), within 12 credits. Costs are A:4, B:3, C:2, D:4, E:3. The current plan is A+B+D. B now costs 5. Replace the fewest checks; among ties, minimize cost. Which plan wins?
questions.explanation: The original now costs 13. A+C+D and A+B+E each replace one check, costing 10 and 12. A+C+E costs less but replaces two checks, so A+C+D wins.

questions.prompt: Each chosen entry needs score ≥8 and errors ≤1. Choose one X and one Y within a new 8-credit budget; minimize cost. Records give score/errors/cost. X: A=9/0/4, C=8/1/3. Y: B=8/1/4, D=9/0/5, E=10/2/1. The old A+D plan exceeds budget. Which replacement wins?
questions.explanation: E is ineligible because it has two errors. A+B and C+D each qualify at cost 8, while C+B qualifies at cost 7, the lowest eligible total.

questions.prompt: A kit must write, scan and print using exactly two tools. Its write/scan tool A is now unavailable. Remaining tools have these functions and costs: B prints, 6; C scans, 2; D writes/prints, 4; E writes/scans, 3; F prints, 4. Which replacement kit meets every requirement at the lowest cost?
questions.explanation: C+D, E+F and B+E cover every function at costs 6, 7 and 9. C+E costs 5 but cannot print, so C+D is the cheapest qualifying pair.

questions.prompt: Period 1 scores rose 40→52 with training and 38→42 without. Period 2 rose 52→65 with training and 42→47 without. A report claimed an eight-point training advantage in both periods. It now emerges that only the trained group switched measurement scales in period 2. Which revision is justified?

options.text: Period 1 shows an eight-point relative gain; period 2 is incomparable
Both periods still show comparable eight-point relative gains
Neither period permits a meaningful numerical comparison
Period 2 proves training caused a thirteen-point improvement

questions.explanation: Period 1 gives gains of 12 versus 4, an eight-point difference. The period-2 scale change prevents interpreting its apparent 13-versus-5 difference on a common scale.

questions.prompt: Arrival minutes after 09:00: before, members 2,6,9,12 and visitor 14; afterward, members 4,8,11,13 and visitor 5. The report included visitors and called arrivals late after minute 5 before, but after minute 10 afterward. Reanalysis uses members only and minute 10 throughout. How do corrected late counts change?
questions.explanation: Exclude both visitors and use the shared cutoff. Only the member arriving at minute 12 is late before; members at minutes 11 and 13 are late afterward.

questions.prompt: A machine doubles inputs at most 5 and subtracts 2 from larger inputs. It then adds 3 and increases any odd result by 1. The threshold changes from 5 to 3; other steps stay unchanged. What does input 4 now produce?
questions.explanation: Input 4 now exceeds the threshold, so it becomes 2. Adding 3 gives 5; the unchanged odd-result adjustment raises that to 6.

questions.prompt: A collection contains exactly three stones: P is marked, blue, heavy; Q is marked, green, light; R is unmarked, blue, light. Colours are exclusive; no stone is both heavy and light. The catalogue claims “all marked stones are blue” and “all blue stones are heavy.” Which named exceptions repair both claims?

options.text: Q excepted from the first; R from the second
Q excepted from the first; P from the second

questions.explanation: Q is the sole marked nonblue stone, so it must be excepted from the first claim. R is the sole blue nonheavy stone, requiring the second exception.

questions.prompt: Cards read A, B, C, D, E. C must stay before D, B before E, and E last. A new requirement places C before A. Using adjacent swaps, which valid final order needs the fewest moves?
questions.explanation: C begins two positions after A, so placing C before A requires at least two adjacent swaps. Moving C left twice gives C, A, B, D, E and preserves every unchanged rule.

questions.prompt: A route must visit K and reach T within 9 minutes. Roads are S→K:2, K→T:3, K→L:2, L→T:4, S→L:1 and L→K:5. K→T closes; all other roads remain. Which revised route works?
questions.explanation: S→K→L→T visits K and takes 8 minutes using open roads. S→L→T skips K, while both other listed routes use the closed road.

questions.prompt: A bill adds a 5-credit fee to a base price, triples the sum, then deducts 4 credits. Its correct total is 29. The fee becomes 3; a 6-credit discount before tripling replaces the old deduction. Any final total below 10 is raised to 10. What is the revised bill?
questions.explanation: Undoing the old calculation gives base price (29+4)/3−5=6. The revised calculation gives (6+3−6)×3=9; the new minimum raises it to 10.

questions.prompt: Earlier surveys found 80/100 weekday riders and 20/100 weekend riders preferred earlier service. Later surveys found 40/50 weekday riders and 30/150 weekend riders preferred it. The report treated the changed overall rate as a preference shift. Giving weekday and weekend groups equal weight in both periods, what rates result?
questions.explanation: Weekday preference remains 80%, and weekend preference remains 20%. Equal weighting yields (80%+20%)/2=50% in both periods; the unadjusted decline reflects the changed sample mix.

questions.prompt: A room must seat 18 people at tables holding either 6 or 4 people. Initially, three 6-seat tables suffice. Only one 6-seat table is now available; 4-seat tables are unlimited. What is the minimum total number of tables?
questions.explanation: One 6-seat table plus three 4-seat tables seats exactly 18 using four tables. Any three-table arrangement seats at most 14 under the new availability limit.

questions.prompt: A routine was recommended to novices and experienced learners. Revised policy requires an observed gain at least five points beyond a matched control. Novices improve 50→64; their control improves 50→56. Experienced learners improve 60→69; their control improves 60→70. Which revised recommendation meets the policy?

options.text: Both groups; both improved by at least five points
Experienced learners only; their final score is higher
Novices only; their relative gain is eight points
Neither group; both controls also improved

questions.explanation: Novices gain 14 against a control gain of 6, exceeding it by 8. Experienced learners gain 9 against 10, falling short. Only novices meet the five-point criterion.

questions.prompt: A fragile, heavy item needs padding and a rigid crate weighing at most 8 kg. A new rule requires a metal exterior. Its current padded wooden crate weighs 5 kg. Which listed change meets all current requirements at the lowest extra cost?

options.text: Padded rigid metal replacement: 6 kg; cost 5
Add a 4-kg rigid metal sleeve; cost 2
Padded rigid metal replacement: 7 kg; cost 8
Unpadded rigid metal replacement: 6 kg; cost 4

questions.explanation: The sleeve raises weight to 9 kg, exceeding the limit; the unpadded replacement fails fragility protection. Both padded metal replacements qualify, and the 5-credit option costs less.

questions.prompt: Four people must fill writer, editor, designer and packer once each. Jo can write/edit; Kai can write/edit/design; Luz can write/design/pack; Mia can write/pack. Currently Jo writes, Kai edits, Luz designs, Mia packs. Jo can no longer write. Which valid revision changes the fewest people’s roles?

options.text: Jo edits, Kai designs, Luz writes, Mia packs
Jo edits, Kai designs, Luz packs, Mia writes
Jo writes, Kai edits, Luz designs, Mia packs
Jo edits, Kai writes, Luz designs, Mia packs

questions.explanation: Jo must move to editing, displacing Kai, so at least two roles must change. Swapping Jo and Kai changes exactly two; the other valid choices change three or four.

questions.prompt: Preparation takes 30 minutes. Then unattended testing (35 minutes) and labeling (40 minutes) may run in parallel. Packing takes 10 minutes after both finish. A new 15-minute inspection must follow testing and finish before packing; the labeler must perform it without interrupting either task. What is the latest preparation start for a 12:00 pickup?
questions.explanation: After preparation, testing and labeling finish by minutes 35 and 40. The labeler then inspects for 15 minutes before 10-minute packing. Total duration is 95 minutes, requiring a 10:25 start.

questions.prompt: A counter begins at 2. Each step doubles its value and adds 1. After two completed steps, the rule changes: each future step doubles and adds 3. Earlier steps are not recalculated. What is the value after two more steps?
questions.explanation: The first two steps give 5, then 11. Applying the new rule only afterward gives 25 and then 53.

questions.prompt: Proposed rules say heat is necessary for cracks, pressure is sufficient for cracks, and cooled tiles never crack. New tests find an unheated, pressured, uncooled tile cracks; a heated, unpressured, cooled tile does not. What is the smallest revision required by these observations?

options.text: Withdraw heat necessity; the other rules remain uncontradicted
Replace heat necessity with a proven pressure-necessity rule

questions.explanation: The first tile cracks without heat, refuting necessity. It agrees with pressure sufficiency; the second agrees with the cooling rule. Neither observation proves pressure is necessary in every case.

questions.prompt: A draft requires a review and approvals from A and B. Absent B is replaced by C, who requires an audit. The chosen review and audit must use different people. B is absent; A approved; E reviewed. E can audit for 2 credits; F only reviews, for 1; G only audits, for 5. C approves free. Which qualifying plan costs least?

options.text: F reviews; E audits; C approves

questions.explanation: Keeping E’s review requires G’s 5-credit audit. F can replace that review for 1, allowing E’s 2-credit audit: total 3. The other options violate separation of duties or role availability.

questions.prompt: Choose exactly three projects within 7 credits. Costs/points are A:3/7, B:4/8, C:2/3, D:3/6, E:1/2. A requires C, and B cannot accompany D. Which valid selection earns the most points?
questions.explanation: A+D+E fails A’s dependency. A+C+E costs 6 and earns 12; C+D+E costs 6 and earns 11. B+C+E costs 7 and earns 13, the largest feasible total.

questions.prompt: Five jobs run consecutively from 09:00. B is third; E immediately precedes B; A precedes C, which precedes D. Durations are A:2, E:1, B:2, C:3, D:1 minutes. At what time does C finish?
questions.explanation: B fixes E in slot 2. A, C and D must occupy slots 1, 4 and 5 in order. C therefore finishes after 2 + 1 + 2 + 3 minutes.

questions.prompt: Before reminders, 40 of 100 invitees replied; afterward, 36 of 60 replied. A comparable no-reminder group changed from 30 of 100 to 30 of 60. Considering response rates, which finding weakens attributing the entire increase to reminders?

options.text: Only the reminder group’s response rate rose
Both groups’ response rates rose by 20 percentage points
The reminder group received more replies afterward
The no-reminder group’s response rate stayed constant

questions.explanation: The reminder rate rose from 40% to 60%; the comparison rate rose from 30% to 50%. Both gained 20 percentage points despite different reply counts.

questions.prompt: A machine starts with an odd positive integer below 10 and adds 2. It triples an even intermediate result but adds 1 to an odd intermediate result. It finally subtracts 4 and displays 8. Which starting value fits every rule?
questions.explanation: Before subtraction the value was 12. Tripling would require intermediate 4 and start 2, which is not odd. Adding 1 requires intermediate 11 and start 9.

questions.prompt: Choose exactly three tools covering writing, scanning, printing and binding, within 8 credits. Functions/costs: A writes/1; B prints/3; C scans/binds/5; D scans/prints/3; E writes/binds/4; F binds/1. Using D requires A. Which qualifying kit costs least?
questions.explanation: A+D+F covers all functions, includes D’s required A and costs 5. A+D+E also qualifies but costs 8. A+B+C exceeds budget; D+E+F omits A. No cheaper triple covers everything.

questions.prompt: In otherwise identical tests, glow occurs with light alone or light plus heat, but not with heat alone or neither. Run three repeats, each using either glowing configuration; exactly one must include heat for calibration. Light costs 4 credits per repeat and heat adds 2. Which description of heat and minimum total cost is correct?
questions.explanation: Glow without heat disproves necessity; heat without glow disproves sufficiency. Every glowing repeat requires light, costing 12. The one required heated repeat adds 2, giving 14.

questions.prompt: Cleaning takes 1 minute, coating 2, drying 3 and packing 1, in that order without overlap. Drying must immediately follow coating and cannot start before minute 4. Starting no earlier than minute 0, what is the earliest possible finish?
questions.explanation: The earliest drying is minutes 4–7, followed by packing to minute 8. Coating can run 2–4 after cleaning at 0–1, so that finish is achievable.

questions.prompt: Twelve people include eight trained people and five volunteers. Every volunteer is certified; only trained people are certified. Exactly two trained people are not certified. Two people are chosen uniformly without replacement. What is the probability that both are certified and at least one is a volunteer?
questions.explanation: There are six certified people, including all five volunteers. Any certified pair therefore includes a volunteer. The probability of two certified people is (6/12)×(5/11)=5/22.

questions.prompt: Buy at most two kits within 6 credits; capacities add. A costs 4 and serves 8 in rain or sun. B costs 3 and serves 4/10; C costs 2 and serves 3/4, listed rain/sun. Repeats are allowed. Which purchase maximizes the guaranteed capacity?
questions.explanation: A+C costs 6 and serves at least 11. A alone guarantees 8, two B kits guarantee 8, and B+C guarantees 7. No other affordable two-kit purchase improves on 11.

questions.prompt: At 5 credits, 18 tickets sold; venue costs were 30 credits plus 1 per ticket. At 6 credits, the fixed fee rises to 36 and one-third of tickets must sell at half price. The 1-credit per-ticket cost remains. What is the fewest tickets, in multiples of three, yielding more net revenue than before?
questions.explanation: Earlier net revenue was 90−30−18=42. New revenue averages 5 per ticket, leaving net 4n−36. Beating 42 requires n>19.5, so the smallest allowed multiple of three is 21.

questions.prompt: Model A uses two red pieces and one blue, earning 5 points. B uses one red and two blue, earning 4. You have seven red and eight blue pieces and must make at least one of each. Which plan earns the most points?
questions.explanation: Two A plus three B exactly use seven red and eight blue pieces, earning 22. Three A plus two B need eight red pieces; the other feasible options earn less.

questions.prompt: Three lamps update simultaneously each round using their previous states. A copies B. B turns on exactly when A and C differ. C flips its state. Initially only A is on. Which lamps are on after two rounds?
questions.explanation: After one round the states are A off, B on, C on. Using those states together, the next round gives A on, B on and C off.

questions.prompt: A succeeds on 8/10 easy and 9/30 hard tasks; B on 18/30 easy and 2/10 hard tasks. A new batch contains 20 of each type. Assume those success rates persist. Each attempt costs 2 credits with A or 1 with B; each failure adds 5. Using one method throughout, which has the lower expected total cost?
questions.explanation: A expects 22 successes and 18 failures, costing 80+90=170. B expects 16 successes and 24 failures, costing 40+120=160. B costs 10 less despite fewer expected successes.

questions.prompt: A program should subtract 2, double, then add 3. Instead it doubles, subtracts 2, then adds 3, displaying 15. The corrected output for the same input selects delivery: scores at least 14 use express (2 minutes); others use standard (5 minutes). Either needs 3 minutes of preparation first. What is the latest preparation start to finish by 10:00?
questions.explanation: The faulty result gives input (15−1)/2=7. Correct processing gives (7−2)×2+3=13, requiring standard delivery. Preparation and delivery take 8 minutes, so start by 09:52.

questions.prompt: Fill writer/editor/designer with different people. Abilities/costs: A edits/4; B edits/designs/2; C writes/designs/3; D designs/5; E writes/2. Only A, C and D are experienced; require two experienced people. Originally C wrote, A edited, D designed. The budget falls to 9. Which valid revision changes the fewest filled roles?

options.text: E writes, A edits, C designs
E writes, B edits, C designs
C writes, A edits, B designs
C writes, B edits, D designs

questions.explanation: C/A/B costs 9, includes experienced A and C, and changes only the designer. E/A/C also qualifies but changes two roles. E/B/C lacks experience; C/B/D exceeds budget.

questions.prompt: Delivery must arrive by 18:00. Air travel takes one hour but requires an unavailable permit; rail takes three hours and is available. Before either departure, inspection, cooling and packing take 20, 30 and 40 minutes sequentially. What is the latest inspection start?
questions.explanation: The missing permit excludes air, so rail must depart by 15:00. The three preparation stages total 90 minutes, putting the latest inspection start at 13:30.

questions.prompt: Everyone following Plan P improves. Nobody using old tools follows P, and each person uses either old or new tools, never both. Ren improved. Which added fact would make “Ren used new tools” logically follow?

options.text: Some users of new tools follow P
Ren knows someone who follows P
Everyone using old tools owns a toolbox

questions.explanation: The added fact links Ren’s improvement back to P. P excludes old-tool use; since everyone uses exactly one tool type, Ren must have used new tools.

questions.prompt: Six tokens are red, and every red token is round. Exactly four round tokens are heavy; exactly one of those four is not red. No heavy token is light. Which report must be false?

options.text: At least three red tokens are not light
At least four round tokens are not light
At most two red tokens are not light
At least one non-red token is round

questions.explanation: Four heavy round tokens minus one nonred token leaves three red heavy tokens. All three are not light, contradicting the upper bound of two. The other reports follow from these verified tokens.

questions.prompt: A counter starts at a positive whole number, applies “double, then add 1” twice, then triples and subtracts 1, finishing at 68. Its start gives the original worker count. One worker trains if that count is odd; otherwise two train. Each remaining worker reviews two files. How many temporary reviewers, also reviewing two each, are minimally needed for nine files?
questions.explanation: Undoing the counter gives 68→23→11→5. With five workers, one trains, leaving four reviewers and capacity eight. One temporary reviewer supplies enough capacity for the ninth file.

questions.prompt: Choose exactly two plans within 6 credits; payoffs add. Costs and rain/sun payoffs: P costs 3, pays 7/9; Q costs 4, pays 8/8; R now costs 3, pays 2/2; S costs 1, pays 0/4. P requires R. Which pair maximizes its lower weather payoff?
questions.explanation: P+R costs 6 and guarantees 9. Q+S costs 5 and guarantees 8. Q+R exceeds the budget; P+S violates the dependency. R+S guarantees only 2.
